decisions.statement: A checkout with no remote has nothing to push to and a missing remote is no failure.
The remote is the remote the branch tracks or the first remote the checkout names.
A HEAD that is on no branch has nothing to push that HEAD as.
A push that fails says the write is already durable locally and only the second copy is missing.
A push that fails tells the caller not to run the command again.
A push is given the time carrying objects takes rather than the time a query takes.

definition: the branch pushed to the remote it tracks, saying plainly what a failure did and did not cost
